text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT SALE - The Canadian Wheat Board sold 250,000 tonnes of low-grade milling wheat to India for February arrival, grain trade sources said. "They've done 250,000 tonnes for February," one source said. "We believe they're working some additional but can't provide enough for the Indians. We have a price of US$152 to US$153 a tonne FOB Vancouver."
CORN SALE - USDA said private exporters reported sales of 102,800 tonnes of corn to unknown destinations for delivery during the 1996/97 marketing year.

WHEAT TENDERS - Algeria launched a tender to buy 100,000 tonnes of French, Argentine or U.S. milling wheat, or any combination of the three, for shipment in February and March, European grain traders said on Monday. Exporters have until 1500 GMT on Monday to submit bids to sell in the tender, which was launched on Sunday, they said. The tender runs until Thursday, they said.
- Morocco will tender Monday for 50,000 tonnes of optional-origin soft wheat, said the state-owned Office National des Cereales et des Legumineuses. Shipment is for the first 10 days of January.

WHEAT TENDERS - Pakistan issued separate tenders for 270,000 tonnes of U.S. No. 2 or better soft white wheat and Australian white milling wheat for delivery January 8-31. The to are be opened at 1100 Pakistan Standard Time December 22 and remain valid until 1800 PST December 23. U.S. grain would be financed under GSM 102. In a separate tender, it invited bids to be opened at the same date and time, for the supply of 270,000 tonnes of Australian white milling wheat.
BARLEY TENDER - Jordan cancelled a December 19 tender for 50,000 tonnes of U.S. feed barley or equivalent origin after buying 100,000 tonnes of Syrian black barley, traders said.
BARLEY TENDERS - The Cyprus Grain Commission seeks to buy 25,000 tonnes of feed barley, with the tender closing December 17 and shipment in January.
RICE TENDER - The Japanese Food Agency will hold an import tender for 7,000 tonnes of rice on December 25, agency officials said on Friday.
CORN AND SOYBEAN TENDER - Taiwan importers could hold one tender for 54,000 tonnes of U.S. corn and soybeans this week, Taiwanese traders said.

MARKET TALK - European flour firms applied for some 362,000 tonnes of exports last Thursday with licences carrying a 26.50 Ecus per tonne refund, EU grain officials said on Monday. The Commission has three working days to decide whether to accept or reject the bids...U.S. grain/soybeans inspected for export during the week ended December 12: soybeans 36.236 million bushels vs 23.100 million a week ago; wheat 17.157 million vs 12.997 million; corn 48.376 million vs 51.737 million; sorghum 5.575 million vs 4.153 million and barley 324,000 vs 342,000.

MARKET TALK - Ukraine's 1996 grain harvest is officially over and stands at a net 26 million tonnes, far below 1995's 36.5 million tonnes, the deputy prime minister in charge of agriculture said on Monday. "We have gathered 26 million tonnes of grain this year, and we can export three million tonnes," Mykhailo Zubets told a news conference. "Most of the exports will be of winter wheat."
